name: Scrange

behaviors.name: Ambusher
behaviors.description: In the first round of a combat, the scrange has advantage on attack rolls against any creature it surprised.

behaviors.name: Bioluminescent
behaviors.description: The scrange either emits dim light in a 10-foot radius, or bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for an additional 10 ft.. It can switch between the options as a bonus action.

behaviors.name: Mud Camouflage
behaviors.description: The scrange has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to hide in muddy terrain.

behaviors.name: Multiattack
behaviors.description: The scrange makes two attacks: one with its bite and one with its tail. It can't make both attacks against the same target.

behaviors.name: Bite
behaviors.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 20 (3d10 + 6) kinetic damage.

behaviors.name: Tail
behaviors.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 24 (4d10 + 6) kinetic damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 16 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

sectionText: The scrange was a large tusk-tailed, reptilian apex predator of Dagobah, attacking its prey with a great ferocity. Scranges were beaked and had many bioluminescent patches on their body, arranged in a ridge along its spine. When prey got close, attracted by the lights, the scrange would lift out of the mud on its six crustacean-like hind legs to make a quick attack or it would use its four tail tusks to impale its prey.
